framework: PTES (Penetration Testing Execution Standard) + OWASP Cloud Top 10
description: External attack surface reconnaissance checks for AWS environments

items.title: DNS wildcard records exposing internal services
items.description: Wildcard DNS records (*.domain.com) can expose internal services and reveal architecture. Attackers enumerate subdomains using wildcard to map internal infrastructure.
items.remediation: Remove wildcard DNS records. Use explicit A/CNAME records for each service. Implement DNS monitoring for unauthorized record creation.

pci_dss.reason: Inbound and outbound traffic restricted to what is necessary for the CDE

items.title: API Gateway stages without authentication in production
items.description: API Gateway stages deployed without authentication allow unauthenticated access to backend services. Attackers can invoke endpoints directly without credentials.
items.remediation: Require authentication on all API Gateway stages. Use Cognito User Pools, IAM authorization, or Lambda authorizers. Enable API keys for rate limiting at minimum.

pci_dss.reason: Public-facing web applications protected against known attacks
All user IDs and authentication factors managed

items.title: Elastic IPs assigned to instances without restrictive Security Groups
items.description: Elastic IPs provide fixed public addresses. Instances with EIPs and permissive Security Groups are directly reachable from the internet.
items.remediation: Audit Security Groups attached to instances with Elastic IPs. Restrict inbound to specific ports and source CIDRs. Consider using a bastion host or VPN instead.

pci_dss.reason: Inbound traffic to the CDE restricted to that which is necessary

items.title: Route53 public zones with records revealing internal architecture
items.description: Public DNS zones expose service names, IP ranges, and internal hostname patterns. Attackers use DNS enumeration to map the environment before exploitation.
items.remediation: Audit public DNS records. Remove records that reveal internal infrastructure naming. Use generic public-facing names. Split-horizon DNS to serve different records internally vs externally.

pci_dss.reason: Configuration standards address changing of all vendor-supplied defaults

items.title: Lambda Function URLs publicly accessible without authentication
items.description: Lambda Function URLs with AuthType=NONE are publicly accessible without any credentials. Attackers can invoke them directly from the internet.
items.remediation: Set AuthType to AWS_IAM for Lambda Function URLs that should not be public. If public access is required, implement application-level authentication within the function.

pci_dss.reason: All user IDs and authentication factors managed and tracked

items.title: CloudFront distributions without logging enabled
items.description: CloudFront distributions without access logging cannot detect reconnaissance, scraping, or attack patterns from the internet.
items.remediation: Enable CloudFront access logging to S3. Configure log retention and alerting for suspicious patterns. Consider enabling AWS WAF on distributions.

pci_dss.reason: Audit logs capture all individual user access to cardholder data

items.title: Internet-facing Load Balancers without WAF
items.description: Internet-facing ALBs without AWS WAF are exposed to OWASP Top 10 attacks (SQLi, XSS, SSRF). WAF provides a first line of defense for public endpoints.
items.remediation: Associate AWS WAF Web ACL with all internet-facing ALBs. Enable managed rule groups (AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet). Configure rate limiting rules.

pci_dss.reason: Automated technical solution deployed that can detect and prevent web-based attacks

items.title: Large external attack surface (many entry points)
items.description: More than 10 internet-facing entry points significantly increases the attack surface. Each additional endpoint is a potential vector for compromise.
items.remediation: Inventory and review all public-facing endpoints. Consolidate behind API Gateway or ALB where possible. Implement centralized WAF and monitoring.

pci_dss.reason: Targeted risk analysis performed for each PCI DSS requirement

items.title: REST API Gateway stages without access logging
items.description: API Gateway stages without access logging cannot detect abuse, enumeration, or unauthorized access attempts.
items.remediation: Enable access logging on all API Gateway stages. Send logs to CloudWatch Logs. Create alarms for 4xx/5xx error rate spikes.

pci_dss.reason: Audit logs are protected from destruction and unauthorized modifications

items.title: NAT Gateway IPs add to public IP inventory
items.description: NAT Gateway IPs appear in egress traffic from the VPC. They should be tracked and whitelisted in partner/vendor allow lists. Unexpected NAT GW IPs indicate infrastructure sprawl.
items.remediation: Document all NAT Gateway public IPs. Update egress IP allow lists at third-party vendors. Monitor for unrecognized NAT GW creation.

pci_dss.reason: Formal process for approving and testing all network connections

items.title: HTTP (non-HTTPS) listeners on public Load Balancers
items.description: HTTP listeners on internet-facing ALBs transmit data in plaintext, enabling eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks.
items.remediation: Configure HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect on ALB listener (port 80 → 443). Enforce TLS 1.2+ with strong cipher suites. Use ACM certificates.

pci_dss.reason: Strong cryptography used to safeguard PAN during transmission

items.title: CloudFront distributions without WAF
items.description: CloudFront distributions without WAF pass all requests directly to origins. Attackers can bypass CloudFront and target origin IPs directly if discovered.
items.remediation: Associate AWS WAF (us-east-1 scope) with CloudFront distributions. Enable AWS managed rule groups. Restrict origin access so only CloudFront can reach origins.

pci_dss.reason: Automated technical solution deployed to detect and prevent web-based attacks

items.title: Public Route53 zone count exceeds threshold (broad DNS footprint)
items.description: More than 5 public hosted zones creates a broad DNS footprint. Each zone is enumerable and reveals organizational structure to attackers.
items.remediation: Review all public hosted zones. Consolidate where possible. Ensure zones not in active use are deleted. Monitor for unauthorized zone creation.

pci_dss.reason: Targeted risk analysis identifies assets requiring protection

items.title: API Gateway has more than 5 unauthenticated endpoints
items.description: Multiple unauthenticated API endpoints significantly increase unauthorized access risk. Each endpoint is an independent attack vector.
items.remediation: Review all API Gateway routes. Require authentication on routes serving sensitive data. Use Cognito, IAM, or Lambda authorizers. Implement API keys for rate limiting.

pci_dss.reason: All user IDs and authentication factors managed

items.title: Attack surface score is HIGH or CRITICAL
items.description: The computed attack surface score (≥5.0/10) indicates a broad external exposure. Multiple public entry points increase the probability of successful initial compromise.
items.remediation: Reduce attack surface by: (1) adding WAF to all public endpoints, (2) requiring auth on API/Lambda endpoints, (3) removing unused Elastic IPs, (4) consolidating public entry points.

pci_dss.reason: Formal process for approving all network connections and changes

items.title: Unassociated Elastic IPs (unused but billed and visible)
items.description: Unassociated Elastic IPs are discoverable but not attached to resources. They waste budget and may be reassigned to attacker resources if released.
items.remediation: Release Elastic IPs not actively associated with resources. Implement tagging policy for EIP ownership. Monitor for unplanned EIP allocation.

pci_dss.reason: Wireless access points managed and documented

items.title: Load Balancer exposes non-standard high-risk ports
items.description: Load Balancers with listeners on database ports (3306, 5432, 27017) or admin ports (8443, 8080) expose backend services directly to the internet.
items.remediation: Remove non-standard port listeners from internet-facing load balancers. Database ports should never be exposed via public-facing load balancers.

pci_dss.reason: Outbound traffic from the CDE restricted to what is necessary

items.title: Lambda Function URLs with CORS allowing all origins
items.description: Lambda Function URLs with CORS AllowOrigins=['*'] allow cross-origin requests from any domain, enabling CSRF and data theft from browser contexts.
items.remediation: Restrict CORS AllowOrigins to specific trusted domains. Never use '*' for endpoints handling authenticated data or mutations.

pci_dss.reason: Public-facing web applications protected against known attacks

items.title: Multiple CloudFront distributions sharing the same origin
items.description: Multiple CloudFront distributions pointing to the same origin can bypass per-distribution WAF rules and create inconsistent security postures.
items.remediation: Review CloudFront distributions for shared origins. Ensure WAF policies are consistent across all distributions serving the same origin.

pci_dss.reason: Automated technical solution deployed to detect and prevent web-based attacks

items.title: No public entry points detected (minimal attack surface)
items.description: No significant public entry points detected. This may indicate a private/internal architecture or incomplete evidence collection.
items.remediation: No action required. Verify evidence collection was complete. If architecture is intentionally private, document this as a security control.

notes: Reconnaissance checks map the external attack surface before technical analysis. These checks identify what an attacker sees from the internet before any credentials are required. Mapped to PTES Phase 1 (Intelligence Gathering) and OWASP Cloud Top 10.
